# Volume 3 — Chapter XXXII Tea with Mrs. Fairlie

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

During the initial Thursday evening that Nell spent at Coombe Road, Thora requested her company at a prayer-meeting. Thora opened up like a flower to go to that gathering. Her attire consisted of a light-blue muslin gown adorned with pansies, featuring a quantity of frills that exceeded anything one would expect from thrifty Thora, alongside a white leghorn hat decorated with three ostrich plumes and pink roses. Nell was thoroughly astonished. At a subsequent time, she discovered the reason behind Thora dressing up in such a fashion—a reason that dates back to Eden.
{: #nw-v03-c32-p0000 }

The prayer-meetings at Coombe Road appeared to be largely made up of women. In addition to the minister, thirty-two women, two boys who were half-grown, and a single man attended. Nell caught herself observing this man. Neither handsome, young, nor graceful, he possessed extraordinarily long legs—legs so lengthy that hiding them required keeping them wound around the base of his chair—and he stooped at the shoulders. He had large hands, hair that needed a haircut, and a messy moustache. Even so, Nell believed his face appealed to her; its quality was kind, honest, and tender, containing an additional element that Nell struggled to pinpoint. Ultimately, she decided that he had endured suffering with strength, an experience that had left its mark upon his features. A kind of patient, witty fortitude showed in his look, suggesting he would endure being burned at the stake if required, yet maintain an agreeable demeanor until the moment he actually had to start writhing.
{: #nw-v03-c32-p0001 }

As soon as the prayer-meeting concluded, the man approached Thora and remarked,
{: #nw-v03-c32-p0002 }

“Am I permitted to walk you back, Thora?”
{: #nw-v03-c32-p0003 }

Thora grabbed his arm, with Nell subsequently mentioning to the young women at Tabby’s Place that it was “with the exact reserved modesty of a sixteen-year-old being walked home by a boy for the very first time.”
{: #nw-v03-c32-p0004 }

“Miss Harcourt, allow me to present Mr. Fairlie,” she stated rigidly.
{: #nw-v03-c32-p0005 }

A nod came from Mr. Fairlie, who remarked, “Miss, while observing you during the prayer-meeting, I thought about how lovely a young girl you were.”
{: #nw-v03-c32-p0006 }

Hearing this kind of statement from almost anyone else would have deeply irritated Nell; nevertheless, Mr. Fairlie’s manner of delivering it gave her the impression of having been given a truly genuine and delightful tribute. She offered him a grateful smile and accommodated him by stepping back on the moon-drenched thoroughfare.
{: #nw-v03-c32-p0007 }

It turned out that Thora possessed a suitor! Nell felt thrilled. Thora was bound to become the ideal spouse—joyful, frugal, patient, and an absolute master in the kitchen. For Nature to allow her to remain a perpetual spinster would constitute a glaring misuse.
{: #nw-v03-c32-p0008 }

“It was requested of me by John Fairlie that I bring you to visit his mother,” Thora mentioned on the following day. “For much of the time she is confined to bed, and she does not ever leave her home. However, she possesses a great fondness for visitors and constantly desires to meet the people staying with me. Are you able to make the trip up tonight?”
{: #nw-v03-c32-p0009 }

Nell agreed; however, Mr. Fairlie arrived later that day representing his mother to extend an invitation for them to come for tea on Saturday evening.
{: #nw-v03-c32-p0010 }

“Oh, why didn’t you put on your pretty pansy dress?” inquired Nell, as they departed from home. The day was sweltering, and poor Thora, amidst her state of excitement and her thick black cashmere dress, appeared to be roasting alive.
{: #nw-v03-c32-p0011 }

“Old Mrs. Fairlie would regard it as dreadfully frivolous and inappropriate, I fear. Nevertheless, John is fond of that dress,” she appended with a wistful air.
{: #nw-v03-c32-p0012 }

A half-mile distance separated "Wayside" from the old Fairlie homestead, which sat atop a windswept hill. Large, comfortable, and sufficiently aged to possess dignity, the dwelling was surrounded by orchards and groves of maple. Neat, spacious barns stood to its rear, and evidence of wealth was everywhere. Whatever the meaning behind the patient endurance visible on Mr. Fairlie’s face, Nell mused that it had not signified duns or debts.
{: #nw-v03-c32-p0013 }

John Fairlie greeted them at the entrance and escorted them to the sitting-room, in which his mother sat as if on a throne in an armchair.
{: #nw-v03-c32-p0014 }

Because Mr. Fairlie was tall and slender, Nell had anticipated that aged Mrs. Fairlie would also be. On the contrary, she proved to be a minuscule bit of a female, featuring gentle rosy cheeks, gentle blue eyes, and an infant-like mouth. Attired in a lovely black silk gown of modern cut, a light white shawl draped across her shoulders, and a delicate lace cap atop her snow-white hair, she could have served as a model for a grandmother doll.
{: #nw-v03-c32-p0015 }

“Thora, my darling, how are you?” she inquired affectionately. “Seeing you once more brings me such joy, sweetheart.” She offered her lovely, aging face for a kiss. “And here is the new teacher. Meeting you gives me great pleasure. So constantly has my son extolled your virtues that I am almost envious, while Thora, I am certain, should be completely envious.”
{: #nw-v03-c32-p0016 }

Unfortunate Thora turned red, Nell uttered some civil and standard remarks, and after that all of us took seats and engaged in conversation. Laborious effort was required, even from Nell, because no one appeared comfortable save elderly Mrs. Fairlie, who assuredly experienced no trouble in speaking. She required Thora to take a seat beside her and touched her hand now and then. Thora remained seated and wore a smile, appearing terribly ill at ease in her awful garment, while John Fairlie remained seated without any smile.
{: #nw-v03-c32-p0017 }

By the tea table, Mrs. Fairlie elegantly requested that Thora serve the tea. Thora flushed even more deeply than before, yet she complied. Nell penned an account of that dinner to Mabel.
{: #nw-v03-c32-p0018 }

“There was cold tongue, chicken, strawberry preserves, lemon pie, tarts, chocolate cake, raisin cookies, pound cake, and fruit cake—along with several other items, which included extra pie—I believe it was caramel pie. Once I had consumed double the amount that I should have, Mrs. Fairlie let out a sigh and remarked that she was worried she possessed nothing to entice my appetite.
{: #nw-v03-c32-p0019 }

“‘I fear dear Thora’s culinary skills have ruined you for anyone else’s,’ she offered charmingly. ‘Naturally no one on Coombe Road aims to compete with her. Will you not take an additional slice of pie, Miss Harcourt? You have consumed nothing.’
{: #nw-v03-c32-p0020 }

“Mabel, my meal consisted of a serving of tongue along with one of chicken, three biscuits, a liberal portion of preserves, a slice of pie, a tart, plus a square of chocolate cake!”
{: #nw-v03-c32-p0021 }

Following tea, Mrs. Fairlie gave a benevolent smile and instructed John to bring “dear Thora” into the garden to fetch her a few roses. “Miss Harcourt will keep me company while you are out—won’t you?” she uttered in a plaintive tone. With a sigh, she made herself comfortable in her armchair.
{: #nw-v03-c32-p0022 }

“Miss Harcourt, I am a exceptionally infirm old woman. I have endured immense suffering for more than twenty years. I have been perishing bit by bit for twenty long, exhausting years.”
{: #nw-v03-c32-p0023 }

“What a shame!” Nell remarked, endeavoring to show empathy yet merely managing to feel foolish.
{: #nw-v03-c32-p0024 }

“There have been many nights where they believed I would not survive until the morning,” Mrs. Fairlie continued gravely. “No one understands what I have endured—no one is able to know except me. Ah well, it is unable to continue much longer at this point. My exhausting journey will come to an end shortly, Miss Harcourt. It brings me immense solace that John will be provided with such an excellent wife to take care of him once his mother has passed away—an immense solace, Miss Harcourt.”
{: #nw-v03-c32-p0025 }

“Thora is a lovely woman,” Nell said with warmth.
{: #nw-v03-c32-p0026 }

“Delightful! An exquisite personality,” agreed Mrs. Fairlie. “And an ideal housekeeper—a role I failed to achieve. My physical condition prevented it, Miss Harcourt. I am truly grateful for the sensible selection John has executed. It is my expectation and trust that joy will be his. Being my sole male offspring, Miss Harcourt, his welfare resides extremely close to my soul.”
{: #nw-v03-c32-p0027 }

“Naturally,” Nell uttered foolishly. She was being foolish for the very first time in her existence. Still, she was unable to conceive the reason. It appeared she had completely no words for this gentle, beaming, heavenly elderly woman who was caressing her hand with such kindness.
{: #nw-v03-c32-p0028 }

“Pay me another visit before long, dear Thora,” Mrs. Fairlie remarked affectionately, as they departed. “Your visits are far too infrequent. However, I imagine John will bring you to reside here permanently before long.” Catching sight of John Fairlie while his mother was speaking, Nell jerked in sheer horror. His expression resembled that of a suffering individual whose torturers turned the rack to its utmost limit of human tolerance. Certain that he was sick, she quickly led poor, red-faced Thora off.
{: #nw-v03-c32-p0029 }

“Does old Mrs. Fairlie not seem like a sweet woman?” inquired Thora, while they walked along the road.
{: #nw-v03-c32-p0030 }

“M—m,” answered Nell absently, while she pondered the reason behind John Fairlie’s expression.
{: #nw-v03-c32-p0031 }

“She has endured awful suffering,” Thora said with deep emotion. “Terrible fits come over her. John remains constantly anxious because of it. Leaving the house frightens him, as his mother might have a fit while only the hired girl is present.”
{: #nw-v03-c32-p0032 }
